title: Cross-domain Governance & Operational Workbook
author: Sana Patel
body:
Overview

This workbook consolidates company-wide policies and operational procedures for access and permissions, change management, data handling, procurement and expenses, vendor management, travel, and internal templates. It is intended as the canonical operational reference for process owners, hiring managers, procurement partners, and auditors.

Scope

- Applies to all Redwood employees, contractors, and third-party vendors with access to company systems or who incur company expenses.
- Includes Hosted API staff, Dedicated/Private deployment teams, platform and infra, finance, security, people-ops, and legal.
- Excludes project-specific security rules subsumed under customer contracts (see related_pages).

Principles

1. Least privilege and role-based access: grant only the minimum rights required to perform the job.
2. Risk-adjusted approvals: higher-risk changes and spend invoke stricter review.
3. Observable and auditable: all access, change, and procurement actions must be recorded in the canonical systems.
4. Centralized templates: use the canonical templates in the Appendix for requests, approvals, and vendor onboarding.

Roles & responsibilities (high level)

- Requester: initiates access, change, procurement, or travel request; provides justification and business owner.
- Approver: manager or director-level approver defined in approval matrix.
- System Owner: service/team-level owner responsible for granting access and verifying least privilege.
- Finance: validates budget and supplier vetting for purchases.
- Legal/Security: reviews contracts or high-sensitivity vendors (data access, encryption, PII).
- Procurement: handles supplier contracting for purchases > $50k and maintains vendor register.

Access & permissions

Policy summary:
- Default access: internal read access to documentation and developer tools; write or admin access requires explicit approval.
- Account lifecycle: onboarding request must include role, justification, and data access level. Offboarding must be initiated within 24 hours of termination or contractor end date.

Provisioning SLOs:
- Standard requests: 3 business days.
- Elevated (team lead approved, business critical): 8 business hours.
- Emergency (Security-approved): 4 hours.

Approval matrix (examples):
| Access type | Threshold | Approver |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| Developer write to non-prod repo | Any | Manager |
|prod data read access (PII allowed)| Data owner + Security | Data owner + Security |
| Admin access to infra | Requires director + Security | Director + Security |

Request workflow (step-by-step):
1. Requester opens an Access Request in the Access Portal (link: /tools/access-portal) with justification and intended duration.
2. Automated reviewer assigns System Owner and records request ID in audit log.
3. Approver(s) review within SLOs; approver can triage to Security/Legal for special cases.
4. Provisioning team executes change; requestor validates access.
5. Scheduled re-certification: owners receive access review reminders every 90 days.

Change management

Change categories:
- Low-risk: documentation updates, non-prod config changes.
- Medium-risk: infra scaling, non-PII schema migrations in production.
- High-risk: database schema changes, model rollouts with user-facing effects, infra network changes that impact multiple services.

Change approval matrix:
- Low-risk: team lead approval, automated CI checks.
- Medium-risk: team lead + engineering manager + SRE review.
- High-risk: product owner + SRE + Security + change advisory board (CAB).

Change windows and release policy:
- Standard deploys permitted 07:00–22:00 local business time weekdays.
- High-risk changes require a documented runbook, pre-change checklist, and a post-change validation plan with rollback criteria.
- Emergency change process: emergency ticket in incident system; post-facto CAB review within 72 hours.

Required artifacts for high-risk changes:
- Runbook (owner, rollback steps, validation queries)
- Impact matrix (affected services, SLOs, downstream owners)
- Backout script and test plan

Data management

Classification levels:
- Public: safe for public disclosure.
- Internal: company-internal, non-sensitive.
- Confidential: business-sensitive, limited to functional teams.
- Restricted: PII, regulated data, or customer data requiring contractual controls.

Handling rules by class:
- Encryption: all Restricted data at rest and in transit must use company-managed KMS.
- Access: Restricted data requires least-privilege and documented business justification; access must be logged.
- Storage: Production datasets with Restricted data require deployment into approved VPCs or private deployments; backups follow retention rules below.

Retention & backups:
- Default retention: 3 years for Internal/Confidential; 7 years for Restricted unless contract specifies otherwise.
- Backups: daily incremental, weekly full snapshot. Restore drills annually for critical datasets.

Data transfers & exports:
- Exports of Restricted data to external vendors require Data Transfer Agreement (DTA) + security attestation.
- Cross-border transfers require Legal review and data-residency checks.

Procurement & expenses

Approval thresholds:
- <$5,000: manager approval.
- $5,001–$50,000: director + finance approval.
- >$50,000: procurement + finance + legal sign-off.

Pre-purchase checklist:
1. Confirm business justification and budget code.
2. Check preferred vendor list in Procurement Portal.
3. Confirm vendor risk level (see Vendor Management).
4. For software with data integration, include Security/Legal review for data access.

Payments & expense policy:
- Corporate cards: policy for allowable spend, monthly reconciliation required.
- Reimbursements: submit receipts within 30 days; non-compliant claims may be rejected.

Vendor management

Onboarding steps:
1. Procurement submits vendor for initial vetting.
2. Vendor risk questionnaire (security, financial, compliance) completed.
3. Legal reviews contract terms (DPA, IP, indemnity).
4. Security performs a technical assessment for vendors with system or data access.
5. Approved vendors are added to the Vendor Register with SLA and renewal date.

Vendor risk tiers and controls:
- Tier 1 (High): access to Restricted data or production infrastructure — required SOC2/ISO27001, annual security attestation, quarterly access review.
- Tier 2 (Medium): integrates with internal systems or handles Confidential data — DPA required, semi-annual review.
- Tier 3 (Low): no access to internal systems, marketing or office supplies — standard PO workflow.

SLA & performance management:
- All Tier 1 vendors must have an SLA specifying uptime, incident response time (initial ack within 1 hour), and escalation path.
- Quarterly reviews for Tier 1 and Tier 2 vendors; performance and risk noted in Vendor Register.

Travel policy (summary)

- Approval: All out-of-region travel requires manager approval; international travel requires approval from manager + people-ops.
- Reimbursable items: airfare (economy or upgraded with business justification), ground transport, lodging (standard business rate), meals per diem.
- Non-reimbursable: personal entertainment, family costs, alcohol over reasonable business meal limits unless pre-approved.
- Expense submission: itemized receipts required; submit within 30 days via Expenses Portal.

Special rules for customer on-prem visits:
- Security briefing required for any employee visiting a customer data center or private deployment site.
- Travel requests tied to customer visits must attach a customer sponsor and statement of work.

Templates & forms (Appendix)

- Access request template (copy into Access Portal):
```
Requester: <name>
System: <service-name>
Access type: <read/write/admin>
Business justification: <text>
Duration: <temporary/permanent>
Owner: <team>
```

- Change runbook checklist:
```
Objective: <what>
Owner: <name>
Pre-checks: <list>
Rollback steps: <commands/scripts>
Validation: <success criteria>
Post-change: <monitoring/rollout notes>
```

- Procurement request form (fields): requestor, business justification, budget code, vendor, estimated cost, contract required (yes/no), requested by date.

Exceptions & escalation

- Exception requests: submit Exception Request Form; include risk mitigation and an approval owner. Exceptions expire and must be re-reviewed every 90 days.
- Escalation path: Requester -> Manager -> Director -> Finance/Legal -> Executive sponsor. Security incidents follow incident response path in security-and-compliance.

Audit & compliance

- Monthly reconciliation: Finance and Procurement reconcile POs and spend.
- Quarterly access reviews: owners must attest to who retains access to sensitive systems.
- Annual audit: Security and Finance coordinate an annual compliance review; evidence stored in the Compliance Evidence folder (link: /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence).

FAQ (quick answers)

Q: Who signs non-disclosure agreements with vendors?
A: Legal signs NDAs; Procurement initiates the request with Legal.

Q: How are travel advances handled?
A: Travel advances for customer-critical work can be requested through Finance with a manager endorsement; accounting reconciles advances upon expense submission.

Appendix: checklists and links

- Access Portal: /tools/access-portal
- Change ticketing: /tools/change-system
- Procurement Portal: /tools/procurement
- Vendor Register: /tools/vendor-register
- Compliance Evidence: /confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence

Document maintenance

- Owner: Finance-Legal (policy maintenance) with People-Ops co-ownership for travel and onboarding templates.
- Review cadence: annual review or sooner if regulatory or business changes require updates.
- Change log: record major edits in the page history with rationale.

This workbook is intended to centralize the operational controls and to be used as the reference for process implementation. For team-level SOPs, refer to the team wiki pages and link back to the canonical templates in this document.
